name: Ragefire Chasm
summary: Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm's volcanic tunnels shelter troggs and a demonic cult. The Searing Blade plots against the young Horde from caverns below the Cleft of Shadow, threatening the capital above.

sections.title: Subterranean Peril
sections.body: Ragefire troggs erupt from deep beneath Orgrimmar into a maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. As orcish builders raise their new home above, the troggs grow aggressive. Magatha Grimtotem sends Maur Grimtotem to open talks on Thunder Bluff's behalf, but the troggs slaughter the envoy. They yield only to force.

sections.title: The Searing Blade
sections.body: A demonic cult called the Searing Blade is more dangerous than the troggs. Loyal to the Shadow Council, the fanatics plot the young Horde's ruin from caverns beside streams of magma. The warlock Jergosh the Invoker, the cunning satyr Bazzalan, and the vicious felguard Taragaman the Hungerer lead them. Taragaman presides over an altar in the lava lake.

sections.title: The Warchief's Game
sections.body: Neeru Fireblade appears to be a warlock trainer beside the chasm's entrance in the Cleft of Shadow. In secret, he leads the local Burning Blade. Neeru sends Horde adventurers into the depths as loyalty tests, hoping to cull weak cultists and kill Thrall's supporters. Thrall knows of Neeru's deception. The Warchief uses these forays to eliminate dangerous cult leaders such as Jergosh and Bazzalan, while keeping Neeru in place to watch the Shadow Council's broader schemes.

faq.q: Where is the entrance to Ragefire Chasm?
faq.answer: The entrance lies inside Orgrimmar, in the underground district called the Cleft of Shadow. It is near the tent of Neeru Fireblade, the warlock trainer.
Ragefire troggs tunneled upward from underground recesses beneath Durotar. Diplomacy failed to quell their sudden presence beneath the capital, which is seen as a severe danger.

faq.q: Who leads the cultists inside the chasm?
faq.answer: The Searing Blade is led by Jergosh the Invoker, a warlock, and Bazzalan, a satyr. Taragaman the Hungerer, a summoned felguard, supports them.

faq.q: What does killing Bazzalan and Jergosh accomplish for the story?
faq.answer: Killing Bazzalan and Jergosh breaks the Searing Blade's active leadership beneath Orgrimmar. Their deaths show the Horde's resilience and let Thrall thwart a demon-worshiping cell beneath his throne.

faq.q: Can Alliance adventurers enter Ragefire Chasm?
faq.answer: Any adventurer can physically enter through the portal, but an Alliance adventurer must evade high-level Horde guards and hostile defenders throughout Orgrimmar to reach the Cleft of Shadow.

faq.q: Why doesn't Thrall simply execute Neeru Fireblade?
faq.answer: Thrall tolerates those who practice dark magic in the Cleft of Shadow, keeping them close and under his watch rather than driving them out of sight.

angles.text: For the Horde, cleansing the chasm beneath Orgrimmar is a trial for young champions to prove their strength and protect the capital.
As a warlock, you can see the dark magic of the Searing Blade firsthand in the rites and demonic tomes used by Jergosh the Invoker and Bazzalan.
As a Tauren, Maur Grimtotem's death at the hands of the Ragefire troggs makes hunting the beasts a matter of honor and retribution for Thunder Bluff.
